title: Everything through inner products
brief: Build the RBF and polynomial kernels, solve kernel ridge regression in closed form, and check the representer theorem numerically.
hints: rbf_kernel is easiest as a squared-distance matrix computed with the expansion ||x - x'||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||x'||^2 - 2 x.x', which needs only one matrix product for the whole Gram matrix rather than a loop over pairs.
is_psd only has to check np.linalg.eigvalsh's smallest eigenvalue against -tol; a kernel matrix is always symmetric by construction, so check that too.
kernel_ridge_fit should solve (K + lam I) alpha = y through a Cholesky factorisation, not an explicit inverse, for the same reason lesson 2 avoided one.

For random_fourier_features, the angular frequencies come from omega ~ N(0, 2 * gamma * I); sample the (D, d) matrix of frequencies and the length-D phase offsets from Uniform(0, 2*pi) once, then reuse them for every row of X.

representer_check only has to evaluate one formula: the squared loss on the first len(y) rows of K @ coeffs, plus lam * coeffs @ K @ coeffs. It works for any point set K was built from, training points or not.
